summary: Intermittent throughput collapse from phased tenant bursting causing fragmented GPU islands and queue serialization in Dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports recurring short windows (30s–3m) of severe throughput collapse in their dedicated pool. Behavior appears as staged or ‘phased’ bursts from multiple client instances that coincide with degraded p50/p95 token throughput and a spike in per-GPU queue serialization.

Impact:
- Customer’s production routes experience 60–90% drop in effective tokens/sec during each window.
- End-user latency p95 increases from ~120ms to >2s, and p99 can go to 6–8s.
- Affects several model routes and causes downstream request timeouts.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity reserved in prod-us-east (pool id: pool-09b7).
- Customer: Maple Analytics (dedicated plan).
- Observed across models: redwood/gpt-6b-open, mistral-instruct-7b.

Steps to reproduce (customer supplied):
1. Run 400 short streaming requests per minute from 12 ephemeral client instances (each opens/closers streams every 5–12s) targeted at the reserved pool.
2. Observe throughput and GPU allocation metrics in the console.
3. Reproduce windows align with external scheduled batch jobs the customer runs (not directly on Redwood).

Observed logs & metrics excerpts:
- serving-runtime logs: repeated entries showing small-batch reservations followed by delayed KV-cache pin release ("kv_cache: delayed_release timeout=30s tenant=maple-33").
- scheduler metrics: gpu_fragmentation_ratio spiking to 0.63 during events; free_slot_count dropping by 70% in 45s.
- autoscaler events: incremental allocations then immediate fragmentation warnings; no immediate scale-down because of transient high queue depth.
- network: no TLS or L7 errors observed.

Initial hypothesis:
Phased short-stream bursts from many ephemeral clients cause frequent microbatch reservations that do not fully release at the same cadence, which leads to fragmenting GPU slot allocation into islands that cannot efficiently coalesce. This produces queue serialization (requests waiting on a small set of active slots) and triggers autoscaler behavior that both over-allocates and then fails to improve throughput due to fragmentation and delayed KV-cache releases.

Requested by customer:
- Immediate mitigation to reduce event frequency and restore baseline throughput.
- Longer-term fix to avoid fragmentation from short-lived streams and ensure autoscaler uses fragmentation-aware placement.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:40 UTC - Triage: Verified customer SLA and collected console traces and pool id. Opened dedicated monitoring for pool-09b7.
2026-03-10 11:15 UTC - Correlated customer request patterns with timing of throughput collapses; events line up with ephemeral client restarts and a nightly batch in their infra.
2026-03-11 02:30 UTC - Observed repeated 'delayed_release' kv-cache warnings in serving-runtime. KV cache pins persist ~28–35s after stream close during events (expected ~5s).
2026-03-11 08:10 UTC - Reproduced locally in staging by simulating 10–15 clients with 5–12s short streams. Replication resulted in slot fragmentation and similar p95 increase.

2026-03-12 14:05 UTC - Temporary mitigation trial: lowered per-tenant short-stream reservation TTL from 30s to 8s in staging autoscaler config; fragmentation metrics improved in staging without immediate regressions.
2026-03-12 16:40 UTC - Noted customer SDK version 2.1.4 used; this SDK aggressively reopens streams without keepalive and can create microbursts. Requested they test a connection pooling patch.
2026-03-13 10:05 UTC - Eng added placement telemetry to scheduler for deeper analysis; confirmed small allocation islands caused by alternating microbatches that prevent large-batch packing.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - Miguel Santos (Support): Thanks Aisha — we have the traces and are enabling extra metrics for pool-09b7. Can you confirm the client's SDK version and approximate number of ephemeral instances?
2026-03-10 10:22 UTC - Aisha Patel (Customer): Customer reports ~12 ephemeral instances and SDK v2.1.4; they also run a separate nightly enrichment job that fires at similar times.

2026-03-11 09:00 UTC - Miguel Santos (Support): We reproduced a similar pattern in staging. Flagging SRE and Runtime for deeper placement analysis. Linking SUP-33489 which contains a previous slot-fragmentation investigation.

2026-03-12 16:55 UTC - Customer engineer (Maple Analytics): We pushed a quick client patch to add connection pooling and saw fewer short-lived opens. Throughput improved during a short window; will run more tests overnight.

2026-03-13 11:30 UTC - Runtime Engineer (K. Huang): Implemented a staging change to reduce short-stream reservation TTL and added fragmentation-aware hinting to the scheduler. Plan: promote to canary for pool-09b7 after customer validation.
2026-03-13 12:02 UTC - Miguel Santos (Support): Customer validated client patch; requesting canary rollout for TTL tweak and scheduler hints. Scheduling a rollback plan in case of regressions.
resolution: Temporary workaround provided: customer applied client-side connection pooling to reduce short-lived stream churn which restored throughput during validation windows. Support staged an autoscaler/serving runtime config change in staging to reduce short-stream reservation TTL (30s -> 8s) and added fragmentation-aware placement hints in the scheduler. Next steps: schedule a controlled canary rollout to pool-09b7, monitor fragmentation_ratio and p99 closely for 48 hours, then promote fix to production if stable. Engineering follow-up: implement scheduler-level microbatch coalescing and make short-stream TTL adaptive based on observed fragmentation metrics (tracked in related PR https://github.com/redwood/serving/pull/2289).
